subject: psychology
title: Conformity & Obedience: Foundations
welcome_lead: Distinguish following the crowd from following orders.
meta_desc: GCSE Psychology adventure on conformity and obedience foundations: definitions and Kelman's levels.
final_note: You can define and distinguish conformity from obedience.

concepts.def: Yielding to group pressure to fit in.
Shared expected behaviour in a group.
Conforming due to a larger group.
Small consistent group changing the majority.

walkthroughs.body_html: Conformity = matching group behaviour, usually unspoken. Obedience = doing what a specific authority tells you. Both can lead to harm, but the route differs: peer pressure vs hierarchical command.
Compliance: outward agreement, private disagreement. Identification: matching a group you admire. Internalisation: genuine, lasting belief change. Internalisation is the deepest form of influence.
People obey those they see as legitimate (police, teachers). Uniforms, titles and settings boost perceived authority. Milgram's lab coat and Yale setting strongly increased obedience rates.
